page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs based on the Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 architecture running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 60.0 GB of system memory. The hardware configuration includes a bundled 1x NVIDIA Pascal P100 GPU with 16 GB of VRAM, 472 GB of local SSD storage, and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between CPU and GPU capabilities. The Intel Xeon CPU delivers modest performance, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core benchmarks falling into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Similarly, memory bandwidth and database operations show weaker performance profiles. However, the integrated NVIDIA P100 GPU excels in machine learning tasks, achieving top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing with 9872.83 tokens/second for a small 135M model and 316.69 tokens/second for a medium 7B model. Text generation speeds remain competitive, reaching 42.77 tokens/second on the 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a specialized entry point for GPU-accelerated workloads without the premium cost of newer-generation accelerators. The primary tradeoff is the older Broadwell CPU architecture and slower system memory bandwidth, which limits its suitability for CPU-heavy processing or high-throughput database operations. Consequently, the ecs.gn5-c8g1.2xlarge is best suited for legacy GPU-accelerated workloads, small-to-medium LLM inference, basic machine learning model training, and workloads that benefit from dedicated local SSD storage alongside GPU acceleration.
